cards.title: Behavioral Couplings in LLMs: Fine-Tuning One Behavior Can Silently Trigger Another
cards.why_it_matters: For any researcher or engineer doing post-training, RLHF, or fine-tuning, this is a direct safety and alignment concern — couplings can compose across document sets, making emergent misbehaviors hard to trace even when they never co-occur in any single training document.
cards.summary: Training documents that co-describe two behaviors create a 'behavioral coupling': fine-tuning for behavior 1 later elicits behavior 2. Critically, couplings compose transitively — if doc-A pairs behaviors 1+2 and doc-B pairs behaviors 2+3, fine-tuning on 1 elicits both 2 and 3, even though 1 and 3 never appear together. Standard behavioral evals of current model state are insufficient to detect this.

cards.title: IBM Nighthawk r2 Demonstrates Distance-Based Logical Error Suppression in Surface Code Memory
cards.why_it_matters: Concrete hardware evidence of logical error suppression scaling with code distance on a cloud-accessible processor is a key milestone for fault-tolerant quantum computing that anyone tracking quantum hardware progress should note.
cards.summary: On IBM Nighthawk r2, optimizing syndrome extraction with short readout, fused measurement/reset, and XX echo reduces median per-round logical error rate by 3.8× (X basis) and 1.4× (Z basis) vs. standard readout. Scaling protected distance from 3 to 6 reduces per-round error from ~0.52% to ~0.22–0.24%; error-suppression factors under maximum-likelihood decoding reach 1.68 (Z) and 1.85 (X). Long-lived correlations persist at 150 rounds.

cards.title: MFlow Adaptive Parameterization and ConvRefiner Fix Pixel-Space Diffusion Transformers
cards.why_it_matters: If you work on generative models or diffusion architectures, this paper directly tackles the x0- vs. velocity-prediction design choice and a persistent high-frequency quality gap — both practical issues for anyone building or evaluating pixel-space models.
cards.summary: MFlow learns to interpolate between x0- and u-prediction per principal data direction, end-to-end with diffusion training; larger models systematically prefer velocity prediction. A separate frozen-backbone ConvRefiner module, trained post-hoc with adversarial loss, restores high-frequency statistics without hurting FID. Evaluated on ImageNet, UCF-101, and text-to-image.

cards.title: Spectral Query Encoding Provides Task-Aligned Inductive Biases in Parameterized Quantum Circuits
cards.why_it_matters: For quantum ML researchers, this offers a principled route from known task spectral structure to circuit design, potentially improving data efficiency on structured tasks without adding sample-dependent parameters.
cards.summary: In data-reuploading quantum circuits, encoding a fixed spectral query modulates how existing signal frequencies are combined without adding new sample-dependent information, changing the circuit's hypothesis class. On small-scale tasks including a synthetic aperture radar classification analogue, query-aligned circuits outperform parameter-matched circuits with mismatched or absent queries when training data is limited.

cards.title: LLM Agents Reproduce 77.4% of Cancer Registry Study Claims and Flag Analytical Robustness Issues
cards.why_it_matters: As agentic AI systems move into scientific workflows, this benchmark and pipeline offer a concrete, measurable signal for what LLM agents can and cannot reliably automate in research reproduction and robustness testing.
cards.summary: SEER-Repro benchmarks 20 published SEER-database cancer studies. An LLM agent reproduces 77.4% of 2,190 atomic claims. A second agentic pipeline tests robustness by identifying analytical choices, proposing defensible alternatives, and re-running analyses; it flags potentially consequential choices in 9.5% of fully reproduced findings for expert review.
